root.name: Slav Defense: Bonet Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Bg5

overview: After 4.Bg5 in the Slav, White develops the bishop to pin or pressure f6 and is ready to meet 4...dxc4 with e4, offering a central pawn for development, hence the 'gambit' label. I only half remember the details of the Bonet Gambit. Black can usually take the c4 pawn and hold it, while White hopes for an open centre and quick play; I would expect Black to equalise.

white_ideas.idea: Pin or trade the f6 knight with Bg5
Meet ...dxc4 with e4 for a big centre and quick development
Regain the c4 pawn later by Nbd2 or e4-e5 pressure

black_ideas.idea: Take on c4 and support it with ...b5
Complete development with ...e6/...Bb7 and neutralise the centre

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4/e4 against Black pawns on c6/b5
Slav queenside with an extra pawn that White tries to regain

character.notes: Unclear from memory; the gambit tag implies concrete, open play with White seeking development for a pawn.

gambit.notes: Name and plan suggest White gives the c4 pawn for the e4 centre, which Black can keep.

soundness.notes: I believe Black can safely hold the pawn and the line is regarded as not fully sound for White; low confidence.

structure.notes: White builds a d4/e4 centre against the Slav pawns, opening the position.

approach.notes: A rarely played sideline; strong players choose the main Slav lines instead.

level.notes: Dubious sidelines are never Beginner; the ideas are straightforward but need care.

character.reason: A gambit of the c-pawn that opens the centre quickly.

gambit.reason: The name and the e4 idea point to a white pawn sacrifice that can be kept.

soundness.reason: Rare sideline, probably unable to prove compensation against correct play.

structure.reason: White opens the centre with e4 and d4.

approach.reason: Seldom played by strong players against the Slav.

level.reason: A dubious gambit cannot be Beginner.

plans.reason: White plays for development rather than long-term structure.
